newsitem.title: USA: Bristol swaps stake to Bass Plc for 47 Holiday Inns.
newsitem.headline: Bristol swaps stake to Bass Plc for 47 Holiday Inns.

text.p: Bristol Hotel Co. said Monday it agreed to buy 47 Holiday Inn hotels and management contracts for another 14 from Bass Plc of Britain for $659 million in stock, cash and debt.
The transaction more than doubles the size of Bristol and makes the company the largest owner-operator of full-service hotels in North America, Dallas-based Bristol said.

Bristol Hotel Company, formerly called the Harvey Hotel Company, owns and operates 39 primarily full-service hotels in seven states with a total of 10,187 rooms. Founded in 1981, the company currently employs more than 4,500 people nationwide.
Bass is a leisure group specialising in hospitality, food, drink, and electronic entertainment.
In exchange for the hotels, Bass will receive 9.37 million Bristol shares, $91 million in cash, and retire $300 million in existing debt. The shares will give Bass a 36.1 percent stake in Bristol.
As a result of the deal, Bristol will become the largest Holiday Inn franchisee in the world, with a total of 84 Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Select and Crowne Plaza hotels.
Following the transaction, Bristol will operate properties in 17 of the top 25 U.S. metropolitan areas. In all, Bristol will acquire properties in 18 states.
J. Peter Kline, Bristol's president and chief executive officer, and John Beckert, chief operating officer, will continue to oversee all Bristol operations, the company said.
Bristol and Bass had said a week ago that they were discussing such a deal.
The combined operating revenues for the acquired Holiday Inn assets were approximately $460 million for the 12 months ended Sept. 30.
Bristol's stock gained $1.125 to $29.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
